sections.title: System design — who owns what, and what fails together
sections.body_md:
**Ownership.** One source of truth per fact; a cache is a reader.

```text
Component     Owns                     Reads
───────────   ──────────────────────   ─────────
<ComponentA>  <fact 1, fact 2>         <fact 3>
<ComponentB>  <fact 3>                 <fact 1>
```

**Interaction.** Every arrow is sync or async and states its behaviour on timeout. NEW marks what this change adds.

```text
 caller                      ComponentA                  ComponentB
   │  (1) sync request  ───►  │                            │
   │                          │  (2) async event  ──────►  │  NEW
   │  ◄──── (3) outcome ───   │                            │
   │                          │  ◄── (4) ack / retry ────  │
```

```text
Arrow  Mode   On timeout                                   On duplicate
─────  ─────  ───────────────────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────
(1)    sync   caller gets Unknown; retries with same key   idempotent by key
(2)    async  outbox row stays pending; relay retries      consumer de-dupes by id
```

sections.title: Component contracts — can the caller ignore a case it must handle
sections.body_md:
### <ComponentA>.<operation>

```python
def operation(request: Request, *, idempotency_key: str) -> Done | Rejected | Unknown: ...
```

- **Outcomes**: `Done(ref)` · `Rejected(reason)` · `Unknown()` — the caller handles all three
- **Raises**: only programmer errors and infrastructure faults
- **Idempotency**: same key within <N> h returns the original outcome
- **Versioning**: <n/a — internal | envelope carries schema_version; v1 parser retained>
